chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayaba who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I borrow a dog from the Magian and hunt with it. So he (peace be upon him) said: Do not eat from its prey, except if a Muslim has trained it and it has learned.

key_terms.الصيد: Hunting/game — refers specifically to prey caught by a trained hunting animal
key_terms.المجوسي: The Magian/Zoroastrian — a member of the pre-Islamic Persian religion that survived in Iran and among some communities in early Islamic society
key_terms.عَلَّمَهُ مُسْلِمٌ: Trained by a Muslim — the condition for permissibility of game caught by the animal

ai.seo_question: Can you eat game caught by a Magian's dog in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that game hunted by a dog borrowed from a non-Muslim Magian (Zoroastrian) may not be consumed, unless the dog was trained by a Muslim. This ruling reflects the jurisprudential principle that the validity of hunted game depends on both the training and the trainer's Islamic identity. The early Muslim community regularly encountered such mixed-religion commercial and social interactions, making this a practically important legal guidance.
